author: Thornton W. Burgess
title: Mother West Wind’s Children
edition: Project Gutenberg 20877 transcription; print exemplar unidentified beyond its undated Grosset & Dunlap imprint. Every selected excerpt collated against the New York Public Library scan of Boston: Little, Brown and Company, 1911, whose title page explicitly dates the volume (Google Books -nE_omvuOj8C, PP11). Selected words follow that dated witness, with verified corrections to the transcription. Straight quotation marks and plain emphasis follow PG; line-wrap hyphenation is resolved and small capitals rendered in ordinary case. Source copyright notice names Thornton W. Burgess, 1911. No claim that the undated PG reprint was printed in 1911. Revised 2026-10-08: Chapters I and III are read to their ends and Chapter XI to its end; these added passages were collated against the 1911 scan (Google Books -nE_omvuOj8C, pp. 8–21, 49–56, 178), with one transcription correction (“your hind legs”, p. 55). Five short sentences in Chapter VII (“Jerry Muskrat saw Blacky the Crow …” to “… and told him.”) fall on a damaged part of 1911 p. 117 and follow PG. Punctuation was corrected to the witness where the 2026-10-07 review found differences (pp. 94, 207); elsewhere punctuation follows PG and was compared with the witness only at OCR-flagged points. Library text: the whole PG 20877 transcription, with the corrections to the 1911 witness that the selected excerpts adopt (listed in acquisition.method) applied in place; text outside the selected excerpts follows PG 20877 and was not collated.

rights.basis: The identified 1911 English text in the NYPL primary witness is public domain in the United States because its publication term has expired as of 2026. Every selected excerpt was collated, with actual differences resolved from page images; PG independently labels 20877 public domain in the USA. No illustrations or later editorial matter are included.

acquisition.method: Downloaded Project Gutenberg HTML pg20877-images.html from the aleph.pglaf.org mirror of the Gutenberg cache and converted with a scratch HTML parser: h1–h6 become headings, p elements paragraphs, stanza divs and br-broken lines stanzas (one line per printed line, indentation dropped), HTML entities decoded, inline emphasis rendered as plain text, prose whitespace folded to single spaces. Omitted throughout: the Project Gutenberg header, footer and licence, page-number anchors, illustrations and their captions (h3 lines under each picture), the e-text credit, the title page and imprint, the contents and list of illustrations, and the transcriber's bracketed query after the printed "somethink" ("[Transcriber's note: something?]", in Why Reddy Fox Has No Friends). Kept: the dedication, the book's title heading, and every chapter with number and title headings. Corrections from the selected excerpts' collation with the 1911 Little, Brown witness, applied as single-occurrence replacements: “in his very deepest Voice and” to “in his very deepest voice and”; “unseen, your-hind legs” to “unseen, your hind legs”; “took her to his storehouse and” to “took her to his store-house and”; “led her to his storehouse and” to “led her to his store-house and”; “tried to hurry that jolly round” to “tried to hurry that jolly, round”; “the old butter-nut tree” to “the old butternut tree”; “and away be hurried” to “and away he hurried”; “"'Fine clothes arc not” to “"'Fine clothes are not”; “curled himself up to sleep, One of the Little Breezes” to “curled himself up to sleep.” with a paragraph break at the sentence end, “One of the Little Breezes”.
